title: Quahog Public Schools
difficulty_source_label: Overall 3, Quant 2, Creativity 3 (1-3 scale); Quant Level - MEDIUM
fit_question: Tell me about a time you persuaded teammates to support your idea. Alternatively, describe a disagreement with a colleague and how you handled it.
prompt: Our client is the superintendent of a system of schools in Quahog, Rhode Island. He is concerned because students at these schools repeatedly perform below the national mean on standardized tests. He has asked us to determine what to do about it.

clarifying_info.answer: A system of schools is a district-level organization, such as Chicago Public Schools.
These are exams administered at a defined point in the school year for a grade level and developed by a district, state, or other large education agency, such as end-of-course exams or the SAT.
On average, Quahog students score below the national student mean on the same assessment.
Teachers and the teaching environment are on par with other schools.
Students come from low- to middle-income households.
Schools provide books to students, but early findings identify a shortage as a major performance issue.

interviewer_notes: This non-profit case tests adaptation, creativity, and structured brainstorming. Show Exhibit 1 before the framework. Explore students, teachers, resources, and the teaching environment, then guide the candidate to the book shortage. Probe repeatedly for additional ideas and encourage roughly three solution buckets. Finish with the Grade 6 impact calculation and a hallway-style recommendation to the superintendent.

suggested_framework.summary: Diagnose student, teacher, resource, and learning-environment drivers before prioritizing the book shortage and feasible interventions.

children.label: Attendance, safety, family obligations, income, language, and special needs
Recruitment, training, retention, and instructional quality
Curriculum rigor, books, teaching materials, technology, libraries, and laboratories
Safety, administrative support, cleanliness, facilities, arts, music, and health services

stages.interviewer_asks: What does Exhibit 1 establish, and how would you diagnose the performance gap?
stages.expected_answer: The exhibit shows Quahog's score distribution centered below the national distribution, establishing a systematic mean gap rather than a single outlier. Diagnose student attendance and demographics, teacher quality and retention, curriculum and physical resources, and school safety and administrative environment. Compare each driver with peer systems and across Quahog schools and grades.
good_answer_signals: Creates three or four causal dimensions
Requests disaggregated evidence rather than assuming one cause

stages.interviewer_asks: Early findings identify book shortages as a major contributor. How could Quahog address them?
stages.expected_answer: Raise money through grants, donations, fundraising, or charging students who can pay; obtain books without cash through in-kind gifts, borrowing from other districts, and partnerships with Amazon or other retailers for used books; and stretch existing inventory through coordinated sharing, scanning, or copying where legally permitted.
good_answer_signals: Uses fundraising, no-cash acquisition, and inventory-management buckets
Generates multiple options in each bucket
Considers affordability for low- and middle-income families

stages.interviewer_asks: What is the total impact of the Amazon partnership and coordinated book sharing?
stages.info_to_release: Grade 6 has an 8,000-book math and science shortage. Math is 60% and science 40%. Amazon can reduce the math shortage by 70%, while coordinated sharing independently reduces the science shortage by 20%.
stages.expected_answer: Math shortage is 8,000 x 60% = 4,800 books, of which Amazon supplies 70% or 3,360. Science shortage is 8,000 x 40% = 3,200, of which sharing covers 20% or 640. Together the plans address 4,000 books, exactly 50% of the shortage, leaving 4,000.
good_answer_signals: Splits the shortage by subject first
Applies each solution only to its relevant subject
States both books and percentage impact

stages.interviewer_asks: You meet the superintendent in the hallway. What have you found so far?
stages.expected_answer: Book shortage is the leading identified contributor to low scores. Quahog can combine fundraising, no-cash acquisition, and better sharing; immediately, Amazon and coordinated sharing can eliminate 4,000 of the 8,000 missing Grade 6 math and science books. Develop a plan for the remaining 4,000, estimate how additional book access changes scores, and continue testing teacher, curriculum, attendance, and learning-environment causes. The main risk is that books improve access but do not sufficiently improve performance.
good_answer_signals: Treats the book finding as preliminary rather than the only cause

exhibits.title: Quahog student performance relative to national performance
exhibits.description: Two stylized score distributions show Quahog students centered below the national performance distribution; no numeric scale is provided.
exhibits.key_insight: Quahog's mean performance is below the national mean, consistent with a system-level gap requiring root-cause diagnosis.

math.question: How many books do the Amazon and sharing initiatives provide?

synthesis: Treat the book shortage as the leading preliminary driver and implement the Amazon and coordinated-sharing initiatives, which together cover 4,000 of 8,000 missing Grade 6 books. Pursue fundraising, donations, borrowing, and inventory management for the remaining shortage, quantify the effect on test outcomes, and continue investigating curriculum, attendance, teacher retention, and the school environment. The intervention may not translate one-for-one into higher scores.
what_great_looks_like: Adapts a diagnostic framework to a public-school system
Organizes book solutions into clear buckets
Gives a concise executive recommendation while preserving uncertainty
common_pitfalls: Assuming teachers are the problem after learning they are at peer level
Applying both interventions to all 8,000 books
Stopping at a book count without stating the percentage
Treating correlation between shortages and scores as proven causation

extraction.notes: The book-impact calculation was independently recomputed and matches exactly. Exhibit 1 is a conceptual distribution comparison without numeric values, so no data table is included. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-09-30.
